rule.statement: A radius-clause breach against an existing confirmed booking is a hard confirmation precondition (17.01.04 C-06), blocked absent a waiver on file. The block's door is a first-class waiver-request instrument against the constraining Operator, on its own clock, escalating on 17.01.03's channel ladder. Break-glass exists only while a challenge clock is live, requires the artist principal in person, notifies the constraining Operator at the moment of use, and writes a named radius-break-glass breach event feeding 17.12.
rule.rationale: 17.01.03's never-block argument was about latency, not permission — 'consent is obtainable, just not within 48h'. Fixing the latency dissolves the argument and lets the tree keep the rule its two other files already assume. Pricing the break-glass (principal-only, injured party told immediately, recorded against the confirming party) is what stops it being a click-through.
break_glass_conditions: a 17.01.03 challenge clock is live on the hold — never on an ordinary confirm
the artist principal acts in person, never a delegate
the constraining Operator is notified at the moment of use, not after
a named radius-break-glass breach event is recorded against the confirming party into 17.12
